text: {"question":"How does the correlation between the deceleration parameter \(q_0\) and the transition redshift \(z_T\) in the PEDE model influence the tension in the Hubble constant \(H_0\) as reported in the frequentist analysis?","reference_answer":"The strong negative correlation between \(q_0\) and \(z_T\) in the PEDE model allows the model to shift the inferred value of \(H_0\) toward the local measurement band, thereby reducing the tension seen in the frequentist 1σ and 2σ intervals.","passage_1_contribution":"Passage A shows a significant negative correlation between \(q_0\) and \(z_T\) in the PEDE parameter space.","passage_2_contribution":"Passage B presents the frequentist confidence intervals for \(H_0\) and highlights the tension between the model predictions and local measurements.","joint_reason":"The correlation in the PEDE model permits adjustments in the expansion history that can bring the predicted \(H_0\) closer to the locally measured value, thus mitigating the observed tension.","same_quantity":false}
